title: Real-Time Collaborative Document Canvas with CRDT
subtitle: Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types (Fugue/RGA) and Peer-to-Peer State Convergence
problem_statement: A Figma-like collaborative design canvas allows 10,000 concurrent designers to edit canvas vectors simultaneously. Using Operational Transformation (OT) requires a single central sequencer, which becomes a planetary bottleneck with 400ms cross-region latency. The system must migrate to a Conflict-Free Replicated Data Type (CRDT) architecture guaranteeing eventual convergence without a single leader.

faded_bug.description: LWW (Last-Write-Wins) timestamp register discards concurrent operations on text sequences, causing text interleaving anomalies.

studio_1_runtime.correct_fix_diff:
+ // Migrate from naive LWW to Fugue/RGA fractional indexing with tree causality
+ export class FugueSequenceNode { id: NodeID; parentId: NodeID; rightOrigin: NodeID; value: string; }

invariants.description: All active replicas must reach identical state vector within 500ms of quiet period.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: What is the mathematical definition of a semilattice in CRDTs? Why must merge operations be commutative, associative, and idempotent?
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: If 500 designers continuously draw lines for 6 hours, how do you prevent CRDT metadata (tombstones and ID vectors) from consuming gigabytes of memory?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: Two users offline on airplanes make 5,000 overlapping edits to the same paragraph and reconnect simultaneously. How does Fugue CRDT resolve sequence interleaving?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: WebSocket connection state consumes 8KB per user. How do you handle 500,000 active connections on a single cluster without Linux file descriptor exhaustion?

counter_probes.counter_question: OT requires a centralized server to linearize the operation log. What happens to local editing latency for users in Sydney connecting to an OT server in Frankfurt?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: Round-trip latency exceeds 300ms, creating unacceptable typing lag. CRDTs enable instant local mutation with background peer-to-peer or edge-delta convergence.
